To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hydrogen solubility in metals substantially differs depending on the saturation method.
hydrogen in metals is localized in high- and low-temperature trapping sites, which is confirmed by the results of thermally stimulated desorption of hydrogen from metals saturated in different ways.

the temperature spectra of hydrogen evolution from metals saturated with hydrogen from media of various states are characterized by the presence of two groups of traps with activation energies of 0.3–0.4 and 1.0–1.2 eV, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the features of the hydrogen trapping in metals.
the features of hydrogen accumulation in the metals during saturation in the plasma, electrolyte and under the pressure of hydrogen.
a comparison of the results of the investigation of the hydrogen accumulation in metals with the features of their hydrogen permeation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temperature of hydrogen desorption in a metal depends on the temperature of hydrogen saturation, the method of saturation, and the metal.
hydrogen traps in metals are filled in the order of increasing temperature of hydrogen desorption, which is the opposite of the order of increasing solubility of hydrogen in metals.

, in the case of saturation from plasma, electrolyte and hydrogen under pressure, the hydrogen accumulation in metals is a multistep process, and the hydrogen incorporation from plasma and hydrogen under pressure is more effective than from electrolyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the temperature spectra of the thermally stimulated desorption of hydrogen in metals are determined by the nature of the metal, the method of saturation with hydrogen, and the temperature of the saturation process.
the features of the hydrogen incorporation into the metal depend substantially on the method of saturation and on the type of metal.
the features of hydrogen accumulation in a metal are determined by the nature of the metal, by the temperature of saturation, and by the medium in which the saturation takes place.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the features of the hydrogen accumulation in metals from media of various states are determined by the specific features of the hydrogen interaction with metal and medium.
the hydrogen solubility in the metal determines the number of traps of various depths.
the temperature spectra of hydrogen evolution in the temperature range 20–500 K are determined by the hydrogen concentration in the metal.
